medications.purpose: Prediabetes/early glucose‑lowering; weight neutral and cardioprotective
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28/PH46 recommends metformin for pre‑diabetes with high cardiovascular risk

medications.duration: Lifelong – review renal function at 2 weeks then annually

medications.purpose: Obesity management and additional CV risk reduction
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46 recommends GLP‑1 RA for weight loss in BMI ≥30 kg/m² with cardiometabolic risk

medications.purpose: Treat obstructive sleep apnoea; improves BP and metabolic parameters
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG38 recommends CPAP for untreated OSA

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive antihypertensive effect; risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury
interactions_checked.action: Check serum K⁺ and creatinine 2 weeks after initiation and after each dose change; hold ACE‑I if K⁺ >5.5 mmol/L or creatinine rises >30 %

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential symptomatic hypotension, especially after first ACE‑I dose
interactions_checked.action: Start ramipril at low dose, advise patient to rise slowly, monitor BP within 48 h

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined diuretic effect → volume depletion, orthostatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Ensure adequate fluid intake; check electrolytes and renal function at 2 weeks

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase statin plasma levels → higher myopathy risk
interactions_checked.action: Use standard atorvastatin dose (20 mg) and monitor for muscle symptoms; check CK if symptomatic
Titrate semaglutide slowly; advise taking metformin with meals

QRISK score not calculated – total cholesterol 235 mg/dL and multiple risk factors imply QRISK ≥10 %; formal QRISK calculation required.
Liver function tests not available – assumed normal; baseline ALT/AST required before statin and GLP‑1 RA.
Allergy status unknown – must confirm no hypersensitivity to ACE‑I, statin, metformin, or semaglutide.
Blood pressure reading not recorded – assume uncontrolled (>140/90 mmHg); obtain accurate measurements before titration.
Genital/urinary infection history not documented – counsel on SGLT2‑i risks and monitor.
treatment_summary: The plan addresses all components of metabolic syndrome: add ramipril for ACE‑I‑based BP control, continue existing thiazide and CCB, start atorvastatin for dyslipidaemia, initiate metformin and dapagliflozin for glucose control and CV protection, and introduce semaglutide for obesity management. CPAP referral will treat OSA. All choices follow NICE CG181/PH46/NG28/NG136 recommendations, with monitoring of renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, lipids, HbA1c, weight, and blood pressure. Contraindicated agents (NSAIDs, pioglitazone, verapamil, diltiazem) are avoided. Assumptions regarding renal function, QRISK, and labs are noted and will be verified before finalising therapy.
